medicina.titulo: Making tumor cells easier for T cells to recognize
medicina.resumo: Immunotherapy has transformed cancer treatment, but not all patients experience long-term benefit, as tumor cells can develop ways of evading the immune system. In his doctoral thesis, Lucas Baldran at the Department of Oncology-Pathology investigated whether changes within tumor cells could improve their recognition by T cells, immune cells that can recognize and attack cancer cells. The thesis was supervised by PhD Jeroen Melief. The public defense took place on October 23.

medicina.titulo: A precision T-cell therapy stalls treatment-resistant cancers in clinical trial
medicina.resumo: Experimental drug invika halts progression of refractory tumors by selectively stimulating tumor-fighting T cells.

biologia.titulo: New tool tracks unintended CRISPR edits and their effects in individual cells
biologia.resumo: A new era of genome research began in 2012 with the discovery that CRISPR/Cas9 could function as molecular scissors to cut specific DNA sequences. Over time, scientists harnessed CRISPR as a genome-editing tool, which held the promise of precise gene removal and addition for research purposes, targeted therapies for genetic diseases like cystic fibrosis or Huntington's, and a future where personalized treatments are the norm. But a major shortcoming has snagged that progress: CRISPR can make off-target edits to parts of the genome never meant to be touched.

biologia.titulo: Soberania genética na arqueologia inspirou criação do primeiro laboratório de DNA Antigo do Brasil
biologia.resumo: Com sede no Museu de Arqueologia e Etnologia da USP, laboratório pretende inverter "lógica colonialista”, criando uma rede latino-americana de colaboração; primeiras análises investigam origens luso-africanas de ilha no Amapá

biologia.titulo: Team develops 3D biomimetic aging muscle model that can replace animal experiments
biologia.resumo: Skeletal muscles, which are attached to bones and enable body movement, are crucial for metabolic regulation. "Sarcopenia," characterized by age-related declines in muscle mass and function, reduces mobility and severely undermines quality of life in old age. However, previous research has been constrained by substantial biological differences between animal models and humans, while conventional methods of culturing cells on flat (2D) dishes have remained ineffective in fully replicating the three-dimensional movements and contractile function of actual human muscles.

biologia.titulo: An ancient virus may help explain what makes the human brain different
biologia.resumo: A virus that infected chimpanzees millions of years ago may have helped shape one of the most important differences between humans and our closest relatives: how our brains develop. Scientists at Lund University discovered that ancient viral DNA embedded in the chimpanzee genome switches off a gene called LINC00662, which remains active in humans and appears to play an important role in early brain development.

robotica.titulo: 28 Zero-Day Findings in Under Two Days. Is Robotics Security Keeping Pace?
robotica.resumo: This article is brought to you by VicOne . VicOne identified an initial set of 28 zero-day findings in less than two days using AI-assisted research across software and tools supporting the Physical AI ecosystem. These include projects developed or maintained by Google, NVIDIA, and Meta, among others. Based on initial validation, all 28 findings are classified as zero-day vulnerabilities. The count may change following vendor and vulnerability-authority review, and some findings do not yet have CVE tracking numbers. Many of these tools help teams train, simulate, test, and operate robots. Weaknesses in them could influence the models teams build, the test results they trust, and the instructions sent to robots. These findings create two demands for robotics teams: responding as AI helps uncover weaknesses faster , and assessing how each one could affect robot safety and operations . What AI changes about vulnerability discovery Vulnerability discovery involves examining code, tracing how systems communicate, and testing whether a suspected weakness can actually be exploited. robotica.titulo: Can Robots Bring Stroke Surgery to Remote Hospitals?
robotica.resumo: I am practicing brain surgery on a patient lying 6 meters away, out of my sight and reach. I press a foot pedal, activating the controller in my hand, and carefully steer a thin flexible tube called a catheter up through the patient’s blood vessels. I head for what I believe to be the brain, tracking my progress on the live X-ray feed. As I imagine finding a blood clot, David Bell , the surgeon seated to my right, helpfully reminds me that every minute a stroke goes untreated, millions of brain cells suffocate, swell, and die . The patient under the X-ray in Bell’s office is not flesh and blood, but a plastic container holding long branches of silicone tubing. The controller I hold comes from an Xbox. But the surgical robot is real. The Remedy N1 is designed for emergency operations, including thrombectomies , the standard brain operation for acute ischemic strokes caused by blood clots. Ischemia, a restriction of blood flow, is the most common cause of stroke. “We want it to feel a bit like a video game—a bit easy,” Bell says. “But we don’t want to dehumanize it as if there’s just another ‘game over.’ ” Bell, a clinician and former cardiac-surgery trainee from Australia, cofounded

robotica.titulo: A shared signal for humans and robots: Flexible display uses both color and near-infrared to communicate
robotica.resumo: A joint research team from the Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology (KAIST) and Yonsei University has developed a flexible display that can communicate information to both humans and robots. Human workers can interpret information through visible color changes, while robots can detect near-infrared patterns invisible to the human eye. The technology could serve as an "electronic tag" attached to products or equipment, allowing humans and robots to monitor work status using the same display.

software.titulo: Alpine Linux Users Urged to Patch OpenSSH Authentication Flaw
software.resumo: A recently disclosed vulnerability in OpenSSH lets an unauthenticated attacker log into accounts that should have no usable password. The issue, named *sshole and tracked as CVE-2026-123158, affects Linux systems running OpenSSH with the musl C library and which don't use PAM. Security researchers now report that attackers are exploiting it in the wild. By Matt Saunders

software.titulo: Apagão da Microsoft: empresa explica os 3 erros que derrubaram 80% dos servidores
software.resumo: A Microsoft informou mais detalhes sobre o apagão global que afetou serviços como Outlook e Teams nas últimas semanas. A pane afetou 80% dos servidores da empresa em todo o mundo entre quinta-feira (12) e sexta-feira (13), o que deixou milhares de empresas sem acesso a e-mails. O Vice-Presidente de Copilot, Agentes e Plataformas da Microsoft, Charles Lamanna, fez um longo post no X com os três detalhes principais que geraram o erro. Um bug despercebido , problemas de tráfego e uma falha que aconteceu nos dias anteriores foram responsáveis por toda a pane. A demora para resolver o problema, segundo Lamanna, aconteceu porque os servidores voltaram a funcionar, mas ficavam imediatamente sobrecarregados. Os 3 erros que geraram o apagão da Microsoft O primeiro problema foi um erro escondido no software dos servidores . De acordo com a MS, uma correção implementada em julho deste ano fazia a estrutura travar em alguns casos. No entanto, os testes foram feitos em máquinas menos potentes, então a empresa não identificou as possíveis consequências nos servidores mais novos e poderosos. astrofisica.titulo: Dirty ice around young star Beta Pictoris suggests frequent collisions and sheds light on the system's formation
astrofisica.resumo: In a recent study of infrared light collected by the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), a group of astronomers detected ice for the first time around the young star Beta Pictoris. Researchers had expected ice around Beta Pictoris, but previous searches had not directly detected it. The study, published in Science, found that the ice is mostly noncrystalline and mixed with carbon dioxide. The team says these new details provide clues about the early formation of the Beta Pictoris system and collisions that may still be occurring.

astrofisica.titulo: Now fully online, the Simons Observatory will shape new studies of the Milky Way and the cosmos
astrofisica.resumo: A new survey of the sky, from the largest structures in the universe to the dust and magnetic fields in our own Milky Way, is now fully underway. After two years of calibration, additional telescopes and a new solar array to provide energy security, the Simons Observatory (SO) in Chile's Atacama Desert is fully online and conducting science operations. Researchers at the Kavli Institute for Particle Astrophysics and Cosmology (KIPAC) at Stanford and SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory have had a hand in nearly every part of it.

quantica.titulo: Reading superconducting qubits while suppressing unwanted state transitions
quantica.resumo: Recently an artificial intelligence proved an 18-year-old conjecture in computer science, called the Aaronson–Ambainis conjecture. The proof settles a long-standing conjecture (educated guess) that eliminates one proposed route to enormous quantum computer speedups, ruling out one particular variant of "quantum supremacy," the term for the hypothesis that a programmable quantum computer can solve a problem that no classical computer can solve in any "feasible" amount of time.

quantica.titulo: Hidden defects return a qubit's lost energy
quantica.resumo: Today, many leading quantum computers are built from superconducting circuits. However, the qubits in these circuits can easily lose energy to their surroundings, scrambling the fragile quantum information they hold.

quantica.titulo: Quantum teleportation method uses weaker entanglement to transfer encoded information
quantica.resumo: Over the past several decades, researchers have demonstrated quantum teleportation, the transfer of one quantum system's state to another, in a range of systems. However, many quantum computers encode logical qubits (units of quantum information) across groups of physical qubits, which makes teleporting the encoded state without losing information more challenging.

inteligencia_artificial.titulo: AI Companies Develop Decision Models to Avoid Hallucinations
inteligencia_artificial.resumo: On 15 September, a startup called TypeSafe AI released a new AI model called Jev . The company’s broad, disruptive claims about Jev that turned heads: The company claimed that Jev, which it calls a “System One model” is cheaper, faster, and can’t hallucinate. TypeSafe AI’s marketing is an obvious shot across the bow of other AI companies and their large language models (LLMs), which, despite their capabilities in math and coding, are infamous for their cost and tendency to “hallucinate” factually incorrect replies. And the startup has certainly attracted both attention and investment. The company recently raised $870 million in funding at a valuation of $7.5 billion . But the most impressive metric of Jev’s success is arguably the many imitators it’s already spawned. Cloudflare, Amazon, OpenAI, and Microsoft quickly released “decision models” that imitate Jev’s capabilities. energia_materiais.titulo: Striped semiconductor panel improves hydrogen production by separating water-splitting reaction sites
energia_materiais.resumo: Scientists from the Institute of Metal Research (IMR) of the Chinese Academy of Sciences have developed an ordered patterning strategy that integrates p-type and n-type BiVO₄ stripes on a conductive substrate. This strategy enables efficient Z-scheme charge separation and significantly enhances the photocatalytic overall water-splitting process. The research is published in the journal Advanced Energy Materials.

energia_materiais.titulo: Scientists propose descriptor-driven design paradigm for battery cathode materials
energia_materiais.resumo: Scientists from the Institute of Metal Research (IMR) of the Chinese Academy of Sciences have established a new paradigm for designing oxide cathode materials. They have moved beyond empirical trial and error toward goal-oriented design using physicochemical descriptors.

energia_materiais.titulo: Researchers develop next-generation bifacial tandem solar cells
energia_materiais.resumo: To increase the amount of electricity generated by solar cells, it is essential to develop technologies that capture and harness not only direct sunlight but also light reflected and scattered by the ground and surrounding objects. In this regard, two approaches have attracted considerable attention as next-generation solar cell technologies: bifacial structures, which absorb light from both the front and rear sides, and tandem structures, which enhance efficiency by stacking two solar cells that absorb different wavelengths of light.

energia_materiais.titulo: Why solar researchers are working to devise a silver reduction playbook
energia_materiais.resumo: Solar power may have become one of the world's cheapest sources of renewable electricity, but an increasingly expensive precious metal is creating a challenge for the industry.

ciberseguranca.titulo: Nova vida nos Galaxy: vazamento revela Bixby 5.0 com memória de IA e tarefas automáticas
ciberseguranca.resumo: Um vazamento revelou mudanças importantes no assistente virtual da Samsung . A Bixby 5.0 deve ter recursos de inteligência artificial para memorizar preferências, entender pedidos complexos e executar tarefas automaticamente. As novidades foram demonstradas pelo canal AppX, no YouTube, e detalhadas pelo site Android Authority. A Bixby ganhará uma função chamada Memória para registrar informações pessoais e preferências, mantendo esses dados como referência em conversas futuras. O usuário poderá salvar informações com comandos, como “Lembre-se” e “Salve”, mas o assistente também será capaz de aprender com o histórico de chats. O recurso ficará nas configurações avançadas do aplicativo e precisará de processamento na nuvem para oferecer respostas personalizadas. Caso o usuário escolha o processamento totalmente offline, as respostas poderão perder parte dessa personalização, já que a Bixby não conseguirá consultar as memórias salvas pela internet. Vale ressaltar que essa função é diferente do aplicativo independente Samsung Memory, também identificado em vazamentos anteriores sobre a One UI 9.5. ciberseguranca.titulo: Vazamento revela "câmera profissional" da One UI 9.5 com modo rajada e pista de vídeo
ciberseguranca.resumo: A Samsung prepara uma grande reformulação no Expert RAW , aplicativo de câmera com recursos profissionais para os celulares de topo de linha da marca. A ferramenta vai ganhar novo visual , modo de disparo em rajada e mais opções de abertura. De acordo com o site SamMobile, a nova versão do aplicativo é preparada para a One UI 9.5 , próxima grande atualização nos celulares e tablets da Samsung. As mudanças visuais incluem novos ícones e atalhos com o objetivo de melhorar o acesso aos recursos, além de criar uma experiência mais parecida com a do aplicativo padrão de câmera. Uma das novidades é um modo de disparo em rajada, ideal para capturar fotos em movimento sem perder a qualidade ou deixar um efeito “tremido”. A função conseguiria tirar até 30 fotos de uma vez e manter a opção de editar no formato RAW. Além disso, a abertura virtual pode ganhar um alcance ainda maior. A matéria original identificou menções a um possível recurso de vídeo, mas ainda não é possível acessá-lo no app. O que é o Expert RAW? O Expert RAW é um aplicativo da Samsung para tirar fotos no formato RAW , muito usado por profissionais por não perder dados por compressão. O app tem ferramentas de controle manua
